rules.name: The canonical name: the key of binaryang's `Features` (`allFeatures()`, `defaultFeatures()`).
rules.cli: The spelling binaryang's CLIs accept, as `--enable-<cli>` / `--disable-<cli>` — upstream wabt's and wasm-tools'.
rules.defaultOn: On in `defaultFeatures()` (wabt's tool defaults; not the same as 'in Wasm 3.0').
rules.implemented: false: the flag exists and changes nothing (see `note`).
rules.requires: The features its proposal states it builds on — function-references 'is based on the reference types proposal'; GC: reference types and typed function references, 'Both proposals are prerequisites'; custom descriptors is 'for WasmGC structs' (its title); relaxed SIMD's every instruction takes `v128`, which only SIMD defines. RECORDED, NOT ENFORCED (owner, 2026-10-24): nothing turns a feature on or off with another and no feature set is refused; each instruction is gated by its own D1 `feature`. So with functionReferences off and gc on, `call_ref` is refused and a GC struct is accepted — as wasmtime 50 and wasm-tools 1.262 do. Which features a TYPE or an ENCODING needs is `typeRules` / `encodingRules`.
rules.typeRules: Which features each value TYPE needs, wherever it is written (a param, result, local, global, table, field, block type). `needs` is a list of groups: EVERY group needs AT LEAST ONE of its features on — [["referenceTypes"], ["functionReferences", "gc"]] is reference types AND (function references OR GC). `needs: null`: no feature enables it, so it is always refused. The rule is wasm-tools 1.262's, measured feature by feature (owner, 2026-10-24); an instruction's own needs are D1's `feature`. wasm-tools also has a `gc-types` sub-feature D2 does not, which refuses GC types when it is off even with `gc` on — D2's `gc` includes it.
rules.encodingRules: Which features a binary ENCODING or module structure needs, apart from its instructions and types — the gates binaryang's validator applies. `needs` as in `typeRules`.
rules.presets: Named feature sets: exactly these on, every other off. wasm1, wasm2, wasm3 are the specification's releases (its change history, document/core/appendix/changes.rst; mutableGlobals predates it, so it is in 1.0); all is every feature. wasm2 is `defaultOn`.
rules.testsuiteDirs: Directories of the spec testsuite (relative to its root) whose suites need this feature. Empty: its tests are in the core suite, which runs with every feature on except as `onlyIn` / `offIn` say.
rules.onlyIn: Absent: on everywhere. Present: ON only in these directories — it CHANGES core semantics, and the core suite (or another) asserts against the change.
rules.offIn: Directories whose suite must run with this feature OFF — a snapshot written before the feature, which it relaxes.
rules.since: The date the entry entered this list.

typeRules.type: funcref, externref — (ref null func), (ref null extern)
typeRules.note: As the element type of a table or an element segment, funcref needs nothing: Wasm 1.0 had it there.

typeRules.type: exnref, nullexnref — (ref null? exn), (ref null? noexn)
anyref, eqref, i31ref, structref, arrayref, nullref, nullfuncref, nullexternref — and (ref null? any | eq | i31 | struct | array | none | nofunc | noextern)

typeRules.note: The stringref proposal: no D2 feature enables it.

encodingRules.encoding: importing or exporting a mutable global
a call_indirect table index in more than one byte (an LEB other than the single byte 0x00)
a function type with more than one result; a block, loop or if with parameters
a struct or array type definition
a tag (the tag section, imported or exported)

presets.name: wasm3
presets.note: Release 3.0's exception handling is the exnref form; D2's `exceptions` also gates the legacy instructions, which no release contains.

entries.name: multiMemory
entries.note: proposals/threads/ predates multi-memory: it asserts 'multiple memories' invalid five times (imports.wast:410/414/418, memory.wast:14/15).

entries.name: compactImports
entries.note: Declared, not implemented: setting it changes nothing, and a module using import kind 0x7f is refused.

entries.name: customDescriptors
entries.note: Relaxes br_on_cast's typing rule: on in the core suite, br_on_cast.wast and br_on_cast_fail.wast each lose 3 assert_invalid (wasmtk, measured 2026-09-28).
